interviews will offer deeper insights into the perspectives of industry professionals lecturers and students regarding the linguistic needs in accounting and the adequacy of the current curriculum in meeting these needs by combining quantitative and qualitative data the study will develop a holistic view of the linguistic competencies necessary to succeed in accounting additionally this comprehensive understanding will enable the evaluation of the current curriculums effectiveness in addressing these linguistic needs and provide insights into potential areas for improvement or modification in the curriculum design to better align with the industrys requirements research instruments questionnaire quantitative data on the existing english competence specific business english needs and learning preferences of a broad sample of accounting students in the state polytechnic of ujung pandang will be collected through the distribution of structured questionnaires interview semistructured interviews will be conducted with a targeted sample of accounting students lecturers and industry experts these interviews aim to collect qualitative data that will provide valuable insights into the distinct language requirements and issues encountered within the accounting profession document analysis document analysis involves reviewing existing curriculum documents and job listings of an accountant profession to find any disparities between current educational offers and the specific business english abilities required in accounting data collection techniques surveys will serve as a primary datagathering method to actively involve a wide range of accounting students by implementing a stratified sample technique the study will give a comprehensive and varied representation of participants specifically focusing on factors such as educational background levels of english proficiency and learning environments the presence of variety is paramount in acquiring a comprehensive understanding of the business english requirements among various student groups interviews will provide a comprehensive approach to gathering data and can be done in person or via video to address geographical and practical limitations the interviews will be organized according to a guide created using initial survey findings guaranteeing that the conversations are concentrated and pertinent the selection of interview participants will be contingent upon their survey replies ensuring the inclusion of diverse perspectives this approach aims to explore further individual experiences and views that surveys may not comprehensively reveal document analysis entails conducting a methodical examination and evaluation of pertinent documents including curriculum outlines course materials and job listings related to the accounting profession and the requirements of business english the utilization of document analysis facilitates comprehension of the prevailing academic offerings and industrial expectations thereby establishing a contextual framework for assessing student data analysis techniques quantitative analysis the statistical software will analyze the quantitative data collected from surveys the data will be interpreted and the significance of the results will be assessed using both descriptive and inferential statistics which will establish a data and identifying common issues views and experiences related to acquiring business english skills within the accounting field thematic analysis facilitates the exploration of the complexities and significance of students needs preferences and experiences yielding comprehensive and intricate understandings that surpass the limitations of quantitative data triangulation the triangulation method
